decision: f-7: where a looping skill link is caught
choice: every Path.resolve(strict=True) in pstack_pin (the installed check, the installer's ownership and skills-dir checks) catches RuntimeError beside OSError, and _stale_homes catches it per home
why: Python 3.12 raises RuntimeError on a symlink loop, so one home's loop escaped deploy() before any other home installed; catching it at the resolve calls reports the existing not-pinned or refusing-unowned error for that home only, while a broad catch around deploy() would hide real bugs

decision: f-6: how a configured local checkout is gated
choice: when the box's factory_root is not the box checkout, the local branch of check() also refuses while the box checkout lags its origin/main, and compares the configured checkout's HEAD with the box HEAD through the existing lag(); no new comparison function
why: the local branch compared that checkout only with its own cached origin/main, so an old clone with an old cache passed; reusing the remote rule gives the same preflight-lagging error, so the waiter requeues with no round charged, marks the box lagging and its idle sync recovers it; the comparison is skipped when the checkout is the box root, so the plain box path is unchanged

decision: f-5: how overlapping deploy passes are kept apart
choice: deploy() holds a non-blocking exclusive flock on self-deploy.lock in the state directory for the whole pass; a pass that finds it held returns skipped before it reads state, fetches or touches orch.db
why: clearing only this pass's own row would fix the symptom while a second pass could still merge or run install-skills during the first pass's install; a blocking lock would stall the timer behind a slow direct pass; this copies the device-deploy.lock and self-heal.lock rule, and a separate file from self-heal.lock means the timer path cannot deadlock on itself
